relevance_note: Two patients with homozygous GAMT variants are described individually: "Patient 1 harbored the homozygous nonsense variant NM_000156.6:c.134G > A (p.Trp45Ter), whereas Patient 2 carried a novel homozygous four-base-pair deletion".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; rows written by a short Python script from hand-chosen spans (spans typed with ordinary spaces were mapped onto the paper's non-breaking spaces by the script and verified verbatim). Labels: text uses 'Patient 1'/'Patient 2' most; Table 1 columns 'Case1'/'Case2' are the same people. Parents are described only as 'both parents' (no sex), so labelled 'parent of Patient N' and 'parent of Patient N 2'; they are in scope as tested heterozygous carriers, 'clinically unaffected' (no feature rows; checklist all not reported). Remaining 48 cohort members (cohort of 50) are out of scope. Sex is not stated for either patient ('individual'). Ethnicity 'Iranian' taken from 'two unrelated Iranian families with ID'. Inheritance: both parents of each homozygous patient are heterozygous carriers of the same variant (parents' sex not stated); recorded as 'inherited unspecified parent' because the enum has no biparental value. Table 1 prints the genotypes without 'c.' ('NM_000156.6.134G > A', 'NM_000156.6.373_376del'); the text form was used. Protein for Patient 1 printed as 'p.Trp45*' in Results and 'p.Trp45Ter' in the abstract; 'p.Trp45*' recorded. Parent variant rows carry only transcript, cDNA and zygosity from the figure legends; pathogenicity, type and ACMG left not reported for parents (stated for the probands' variants). Functional evidence: the paper states functional assays were not performed (in silico predictions only), recorded as not reported. Normal findings: 'Cranial MRI and CT were (reported as) normal' recorded as excluded 'abnormal cranial MRI'/'abnormal cranial CT' (whole investigation, D-27); the three MRI checklist items were left not reported because a normal investigation as a whole excludes nothing more specific. Table 1 symbols '−' and 'N' are not defined in the legend, so they were not used to exclude anything; exclusions (hypotonia, clonus, Babinski) come from the text. Contradictions/oddities: Table 1 gives Patient 1 urine GAA and urine creatine as '−', but the text says 'Urinary GAA and urinary creatine measurements were not available for either patient' (not recorded). Patient 2 touch hypersensitivity is '−' in Table 1 and 'not reported' in the text: no row. Patient 2's DTR '+2' is described in the text as 'increased'; recorded as stated. Conclusion says 'one novel pathogenic variants ... in two unrelated Iranian families'. 'absent or limited speech' marked observed from 'severe impairment of expressive and cognitive speech'; 'stereotypies' from 'repetitive hand-flapping'. Treatment: 'Detailed treatment history and longitudinal follow-up data were unavailable' (not reported). No ages at onset or diagnosis given; ages 14 and 17 recorded as age at report. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper says the c.134G>A variant was previously reported, not these patients. Consanguinity not stated for these families.
